short: Time evolution on same-spin antisymmetric grid states

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPower_correctness
lean.plain: One compiled unitary for every spin partition
lean.annotation: The same $W$ appears in both conjuncts of `stoppingPower_correctness`. The first compares $W$ with the target evolution in each spin sector. The second requires the compiled circuit, including any mid-circuit measurements and feed-forward, to realize the action of that $W$ on valid grid inputs with clean ancillas.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Algorithms.StoppingPower:QuantumComputation.Specs.ApproximatesTimeEvolution
lean.annotation: In `ApproximatesTimeEvolution` the zero-ancilla projector multiplies the operator difference on the right and fixes the input. The norm is on the joint output, so any amplitude in a nonzero ancilla state contributes to the error. The ideal output has ancillas in $|0\rangle^{\otimes m}$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.fermionicProjector
lean.annotation: `spinUp` is the set of spin-up registers, and the other registers are spin-down. The condition `g i ∈ spinUp ↔ i ∈ spinUp` allows permutation of electrons within each set. If the first set has size $s$, there are $s!(218-s)!$ such permutations, the denominator of the signed average.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPowerSolution.ComposableLiveEndpoint.gqsp_hTotErr11
lean.plain: Total error at most 10⁻² for each evolution time
lean.annotation: Among the ten certified upper bounds in `gqsp_hTotErr11`, the largest is at $t=3$. Three segment errors contribute about $0.000391997217$, the block-encoding term contributes $0.009607998$, and phase-gradient preparation and its inverse together contribute $4.6\times10^{-9}$. Their sum is about $0.009999999817$, below $10^{-2}$.

lean.name: RealizesUnitaryFromBasisOutcomesAndZeroWorkspace
lean.plain: Unitary realization on selected basis inputs
lean.annotation: `restrictToZeroAncilla` fixes the workspace independently of `restrictToBasisOutcomes`, which allows superpositions of valid grid states. Every run therefore begins with zero workspace. The circuit prepares its own phase-gradient state during initialization and applies the inverse preparation during cleanup.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPower_correctness
lean.plain: One compiled unitary for every spin partition
lean.annotation: For each allowed configuration, time and disjoint register placement, the compiled circuit realizes one unitary $W$ on all valid grid inputs with zero ancillas. The bound on the difference from $e^{-iHt}$ applies to the smaller subspace of grid states antisymmetric under same-spin exchange. Within each spin partition, one phase applies to all vectors in that subspace.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Algorithms.StoppingPower:QuantumComputation.Specs.ApproximatesTimeEvolution
lean.annotation: The factor `input` on the right projects onto the selected spin sector and the all-zero ancilla state. The operator norm of the restricted difference is the largest vector error over unit inputs in that subspace. The output vector includes the ancillas, so the bound also controls any component with nonzero output ancillas.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.fermionicProjector
lean.annotation: Multiplying `fermionicProjector` by a same-spin exchange reindexes the signed permutation sum and reverses every sign. A vector in the range therefore changes sign under that exchange. Applying the same one-electron basis change to all electron registers commutes with the exchanges, so the antisymmetry condition persists in the position basis.

lean.name: RealizesUnitaryFromBasisOutcomesAndZeroWorkspace
lean.plain: Unitary realization on selected basis inputs
lean.annotation: For each joint output observable $M$, Lean compares the program's weakest precondition with $W^\dagger M W$. It applies the same input projector to both expressions, then requires the program's expression to be at least as large in the positive-semidefinite order. The quantifier includes observables with off-diagonal entries, so the statement checks coherence between valid momentum configurations as well as their outcome probabilities.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Algorithms.StoppingPower:QuantumComputation.Specs.ApproximatesTimeEvolution
lean.annotation: The phase $\varphi$ is chosen before taking the operator norm, so it is fixed across all input vectors of the given spin partition. Adding a scalar $cI$ to the Hamiltonian multiplies $e^{-iHt}$ by $e^{-ict}$, which can be absorbed into this phase. This is the freedom used when Appendix G.3 reproduces the interaction up to a constant.
